title: Schotter drift
label: A lattice of squares where order and disorder trade places in drifting patches, some squares opening into nested ones, while slow rings of order cross the sheet.

title: Ruled disorder
label: Bands of short strokes slide past one another, each band drifting between one strict direction and a mix of verticals and diagonals, while a travelling gap parts the strokes around a moving point.

title: Trames moire
label: Two sets of fine concentric rings with slightly shifted centres overprint inside a disc; the interference pattern sweeps across as the two centres circle in opposite directions.

title: Tesseract
label: A hypercube turning in four dimensions, projected to a fan of fine lines where only a seeded subset of its edges is drawn.

title: Hairline flow
label: Thousands of fine hairlines combed along a slowly drifting flow field that bends around an empty disc.

title: Ribbon sheaf
label: One looping curve copied a few hundred times, each copy turned slightly further, so the hairlines build a folded translucent ribbon.

title: Iso-bands
label: Evenly spaced contour lines of a slowly drifting warped field, splitting and merging like the bands of a topographic map.

title: Glyph tiling
label: A sheet of square tiles each holding quarter-curve ribbons of hairlines that meet across the edges, sliding slowly; different rules set the tile directions in different regions, the curves straighten into diamonds around a wandering point, and slow fronts half-turn some tiles.

title: Pegs and string
label: A single thin string wound around a lattice of pegs, drawn as straight tangents and small wraps, that keeps circling loose around its pegs in a wave from left to right.

title: Metamorphosis
label: A sheet of hatched and empty tiles that interlock without gaps and drift sideways; their edge curves change from one shape family to another as they cross the page.

title: Harmonograph
math: x(t) = Σ A_i sin(f_i t + φ_i) e^(-d_i t), y(t) likewise; f_i near integer ratios, e.g. 3 : 2 + 0.02
label: A pen traced by damped pendulums: near-integer frequency ratios make a decaying spiral whose ink gathers where the path retraces.
